sections.html:
The number of described Sternarchorhynchus species has risen enormously in recent years. Up to 1994 only 4 species were known, in 2006 the number had increased to 10, and by 2014 32 species were accepted. This makes Sternarchorhynchus the most species-rich genus of the Apteronotidae. The main differences between the species lie in the shape of the snout.

When these fish first arrived only a quite rough determination was possible, so they were listed as S. mormyrus. Analysis of photos makes it much more likely that they are S. goeldii, a species described only in 2010. S. mormyrus reaches about 50 cm, S. goeldii about 30 cm.
Feeding Sternarchorhynchus in aquaria is no problem: the fish readily take any type of live and frozen food.

The animals are a bit quarrelsome towards each other, but they do not hurt their counterpart. They swim around each other with high speed and breathtaking elegance, and the better swimmer wins the combat. The snout plays a special role during these fights: the fish use it like the sword of a foil fencer.

Sternarchorhynchus means "snout with the anus at the breast"; this refers to the long snout and to the fact that in Sternarchorhynchus the anus is placed immediately behind the head. mormyrus means "mormyrid"; the members of the African fish genus Mormyrus have a comparably long snout. goeldii is a dedication name for Emilio (actually Emil) Goeldi (1859-1917), in appreciation of his merits regarding the knowledge of the animals of Amazonia.
